subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Mentor's notebook. Written by Mohit.
Met Sudha for our monthly coffee today. She was promoted to operations lead two months ago, and she's doing well: costs down, the delivery backlog cleared.
But I noticed it in the quarterly review last week and again today. 'I cut the costs.' 'I fixed the backlog.' 'I renegotiated the courier deal.' Every win, I. At the review, two people from her team glanced at each other when she said it. I don't think she saw.
I know that glow. I had it too, the year I was promoted.
Today, walking back to the car, I said quietly, 'Can I tell you something as a friend? Your team is noticing the "I". The backlog was Neeraj and Shobha as much as you.'
She stopped. Her face went tight for a second. Then she said, 'Oh. Oh no. You're right.' She thanked me before she got in the car.

qa.q: What was Sudha promoted to two months ago?
qa.a: She was promoted to operations lead two months ago.

qa.q: How did Sudha feel when Mohit mentioned the 'I', and how can you tell?
qa.a: She was stung at first, as her face went tight, and then embarrassed and grateful as she realised it was true.

qa.q: Why did Mohit's remark work, and what made the timing and place right?
qa.a: It was private, kind and specific, naming Neeraj and Shobha, so Sudha could hear it without losing face in front of her team.

qa.q: How might Neeraj and Shobha feel if Sudha starts crediting them by name?
qa.a: They are likely to feel seen and more willing to keep giving their best to her team.

grounding: It shows a mentor who notices a newly promoted friend claiming team wins as her own and offers a private, kind remark that the team has noticed.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Saturday
Aadhya called tonight, happy, to tell me about the client presentation. It went well. I'm glad. But I counted, somewhere in the middle: 'my strategy', 'my deck', 'I closed it', 'I told them'. Maybe fourteen times. Her team of five did most of that deck. I know, because Leena was up till two on it and texted me.
Two months ago Aadhya was the person who always said 'we'. The promotion's changed something.
I almost said nothing. It isn't my business, and she's so happy.
But I remember what happened to Suresh in my old office. His team simply stopped trying, and nobody told him why until it was too late.
So at the end of the call I said, 'Can I say one small thing, as your friend? Your team might be hearing a lot of "I" lately.'
She went quiet. Then: 'Yash. Seriously?' A pause. 'Okay. Tell me more.'

qa.q: How many people are on Aadhya's team?
qa.a: Her team has five people.

qa.q: What was Yash worried about before deciding to speak up?
qa.a: Yash worried it wasn't Yash's business and might spoil Aadhya's happiness, but feared her team would stop trying, like Suresh's did.

qa.q: What made Yash's remark a good way to raise the problem?
qa.a: It was private, framed as coming from a friend, and short, which let Aadhya ask for more instead of feeling attacked.

qa.q: How might Leena feel if Aadhya starts saying 'we' again about the deck?
qa.a: Leena would likely feel her late nights were noticed and valued, and trust Aadhya more.

grounding: It shows a friend noticing a newly promoted person speaking in the first person about team wins and choosing to mention it privately and kindly.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
At the panchayat function, the new cluster coordinator, Anand, stood at the microphone and talked about the rainwater tanks in the three village schools. "I planned them, I got the funds, I supervised the work," he said, and the sarpanch clapped.
Pradeep, the old headmaster who had trained Anand as a young teacher, sat in the second row and watched the three teachers at the back. Lakshmi had dug with the children every Saturday. Babu had fought the contractor for proper pipes. Both were looking at their feet.
After the function, while everyone queued for tea, Pradeep walked with Anand behind the school wall.
"I'm proud of you, beta. But one thing, only between us. Today it was I, I, I. Lakshmi and Babu heard it. People forgive a young leader many things, but they remember who took the credit."
Anand was quiet for a long moment. Then he nodded and walked back towards the teachers with two cups of tea.

qa.q: What did Babu fight the contractor for?
qa.a: Proper pipes.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling as he watched the teachers at the back?
qa.a: He felt uneasy and protective, worried that Anand's 'I, I, I' was hurting the teachers and could damage his future.

qa.q: Why did Pradeep speak behind the school wall instead of at the function?
qa.a: A private, kind word lets Anand hear the warning without public shame, so he can make it right with the teachers.

qa.q: What was the speech like for Lakshmi and Babu?
qa.a: They likely felt hurt and invisible, their Saturdays and fights with the contractor swallowed into someone else's 'I'.

grounding: An old headmaster sees a newly promoted former pupil take credit for the team's work and quietly warns him in private.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Selin had mentored Emeka since his first week at the shipping office in Istanbul, and she had cheered loudest when he was made team lead in spring. So she noticed first.
At the quarterly review Emeka presented the new route plan that had cut delays by a third. "I spotted the bottleneck at the port," he said. "I designed the new schedule. I negotiated with the carriers." Behind him, on the slide, was the team photo. Deniz, who had actually spotted the bottleneck, kept smiling at the table, but the smile went thin.
Afterwards Selin asked Emeka to walk to the ferry with her. The Bosphorus was grey and choppy.
"You deserve that promotion," she said. "And I'm telling you this as your friend, not your senior. People noticed the 'I' today. Deniz noticed."
Emeka stopped walking. "Was it that bad?"
"Not yet," Selin said. "That's why I'm saying it now."

qa.q: By how much did the new route plan cut delays?
qa.a: By a third.

qa.q: What was Selin thinking when she asked Emeka to walk to the ferry?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and caring, wanting to warn him privately before the credit-taking hurt his reputation.

qa.q: What makes Selin's approach wise?
qa.a: She affirms his promotion, speaks as a friend in private, and names a specific person who noticed, so he can act on it.

qa.q: What might Deniz have felt during the presentation?
qa.a: Deniz likely felt overlooked and hurt, watching a personal discovery presented as Emeka's.

grounding: A mentor notices a newly promoted friend presenting team wins in the first person and gives a private, kind warning.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage: The quarterly town hall at the software firm ran long, and Harsha stood at the back with his coffee. Karthik, promoted to project head six weeks earlier, was presenting the delivery that the whole team had sweated over. "I rebuilt the timeline. I pushed the client. I got us there." Harsha counted: eleven "I"s in four minutes, not one name. Near him, two developers exchanged a look, and one quietly closed her laptop. Harsha had mentored Karthik since his first internship and liked him enormously. After the session he found Karthik by the lifts. "Walk with me a minute?" In the stairwell, away from everyone, he kept his voice low. "You did well today. But the team is noticing that it's all 'I' now. They were there too." Karthik's smile slipped. "I didn't mean it like that." "I know. That's why I'm telling you here."

qa.q: How many times did Harsha count Karthik saying I?
qa.a: Harsha counted eleven I's in four minutes, with not one name.

qa.q: Why does Harsha choose the stairwell to talk to Karthik?
qa.a: Harsha cares about Karthik and is worried for him, so he wants to warn him privately without embarrassing him in front of others.

qa.q: What makes Harsha's approach likely to work at this stage?
qa.a: Harsha is kind, specific and private: he praises the work, names the one habit the team is noticing, and speaks early before resentment sets in.

qa.q: What might Karthik be feeling when his smile slips?
qa.a: Karthik may feel stung and embarrassed, since he believed he was just proudly reporting a win, not taking credit from the team.
